c.tagline: Ancient dynastic capital of the Longmen grottoes, white horses, and peonies.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis use meters; carry the destination written in Chinese as few drivers speak English, or hail through Didi in-app.

emergency.note: 110 reaches the police and 120 reaches medical/ambulance services; 119 is the fire brigade.

avoid.reason: Touts and unofficial 'guides' around Longmen Grottoes and the railway stations — buy tickets at official counters.

hood_desc: The historic Old Town (Laocheng) around the Drum Tower, Lijing Gate, and the restored Luoyi Ancient City lanes; best for first-timers who want atmospheric streets, night markets, and traditional guesthouses near the sights.
The central Xigong District around Wangcheng Park and the main railway station, a busy commercial base with shopping, restaurants, and good metro and bus links to the rest of the city.
The western Jianxi District, a modern business and shopping area with reliable mid-range hotels and easy access west of the center; a practical, calmer base for longer stays.

The Luolong New District south of the Luo River, home to newer high-rise hotels, the Longmen high-speed railway station, and quick access to the Longmen Grottoes; suits travelers prioritizing the UNESCO caves.
The leafy Wangcheng Park area, the heart of the annual Peony Festival, with gardens, boulevards, and quieter residential streets; a green base especially popular in peony season.
lodging: The Reserve Hotel Luoyang, Curio Collection by Hilton
Hilton Garden Inn Luoyang Kaiyuan Avenue

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water only, as throughout China.

transit.hours: The metro runs roughly 6:30 AM to 10:30 PM; city buses generally operate from early morning until around 9:00-10:00 PM.
transit.note: The Luoyang Subway opened in 2021 and has two lines: Line 1 runs east–west past Wangcheng Park and the Luoyi Ancient City, and Line 2 runs north–south to the main and Longmen high-speed railway stations. An extensive city bus network fills in the rest.
transit.pay: Pay with a rechargeable transit card, a mobile QR code (Alipay/WeChat), or cash on buses. Metro fares are distance-based and bought at station machines.

bus: Long-distance coaches to Zhengzhou, Dengfeng (Shaolin), and across Henan

car.idp: Not valid; a temporary Chinese license is required to drive

train: Luoyang Railway Station and Luoyang Longmen high-speed station (frequent high-speed services to Zhengzhou, Xi'an, and Beijing)

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to city center (~30-40 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected in restaurants, taxis, or hotels.

food.name: Luoyang Water Banquet (shuixi)
food.desc: A thousand-year-old Tang dynasty feast of 24 courses served one after another like flowing water, every hot dish arriving in its own soup or broth.

places.name: Zhenbutong Restaurant
places.note: The official water banquet house since a 1973 state banquet; order a la carte if the full 24 courses is too much.

places.name: Guanji Water Banquet
places.note: Long-running family rival to Zhenbutong, cheaper and popular with Luoyang residents.

places.name: Restaurants along Lijing Gate food street
places.note: Several old-town restaurants offer shortened water banquet sets for two or four people.

food.name: Luoyang Yancai (peony swallow dish)
food.desc: The banquet's opening course: white radish cut into threads so fine it imitates birds nest, in a clear sour-savoury broth topped with a carved peony.

places.name: Zhenbutong Restaurant
places.note: The version that made the dish famous, plated with the signature peony flower on top.

places.name: Guanji Water Banquet
places.note: Same classic done for a local crowd, and available as a single dish rather than a set.

places.name: Restaurants at Luoyi Ancient City
places.note: Restored old-city dining quarter where several kitchens serve banquet dishes individually.

food.name: Luoyang niurou tang (beef soup)
food.desc: Luoyang's breakfast: beef bones simmered overnight into a peppery, oily broth, poured over sliced beef and torn flatbread with coriander and chilli oil.

places.name: Beef soup shops around Shizi Street
places.note: The old-town crossroads has several shops open from around 5am; go early before the pot runs down.

places.name: Shizijie Night Market
places.note: Late-night version of the same soup, alongside skewers and street snacks.

places.name: Soup stalls near Lijing Gate
places.note: Convenient for visitors staying near the old city gate, with English picture menus at some counters.

food.name: Bufan tang
food.desc: A Luoyang-only soup: thin millet pancakes floated on a sour, peppery broth with vermicelli, tofu skin, seaweed and pork, eaten piping hot.

places.name: Bufan tang shops on Shizi Street
places.note: The dish is a Luoyang intangible heritage item and these old-town shops are where locals eat it.

places.name: Shizijie Night Market
places.note: Easy place to try a small bowl among many other snacks without committing to a full meal.

places.name: Luoyi Ancient City food lanes
places.note: Tourist-friendly stalls with picture menus, handy if you do not read Chinese.

food.name: Jiang mian tiao
food.desc: Noodles cooked in fermented mung bean whey until tangy and slightly thick, topped with celery, soybeans and chilli oil; the local comfort bowl.

places.name: Noodle shops around Shizi Street
places.note: Small family shops in the old town make the whey themselves, which is what gives the sourness.

places.name: Shizijie Night Market
places.note: Sold cheaply by the bowl in the evening, a good pairing with a skewer or two.

places.name: Restaurants along Lijing Gate food street
places.note: Several sit-down places list it alongside water banquet dishes for a lighter meal.

food.name: Mudan bing (peony cake)
food.desc: Flaky pastry rounds filled with peony petal, rose or red bean paste, made in the city that has grown peonies since the Tang dynasty.

places.name: Pastry shops at Lijing Gate
places.note: Sold warm from the tray and boxed for gifts; peak season is the April peony festival.

places.name: Luoyi Ancient City shops
places.note: Several confectioners here bake them on site so you can watch the folding.

places.name: Shizijie Night Market
places.note: Cheapest place to buy a few singles rather than a whole presentation box.

food.name: Dukang jiu
food.desc: Grain spirit from the Luoyang countryside named after Dukang, the legendary inventor of Chinese wine; strong, sorghum-based and poured in small cups.

places.name: Zhenbutong Restaurant
places.note: Stocks the local baijiu as the traditional accompaniment to a water banquet.

places.name: Restaurants along Lijing Gate food street
places.note: Old-town restaurants pour it by the small carafe with dinner.

places.name: Shops at Luoyi Ancient City
places.note: Souvenir liquor shops sell bottles of the regional brand to take home.

food.name: Mudan hua cha (peony flower tea)
food.desc: Dried peony buds steeped into a pale, floral infusion, sometimes blended with chrysanthemum or rock sugar; a Luoyang speciality tied to the peony gardens.

places.name: Tea houses at Luoyi Ancient City
places.note: Courtyard tea houses serve it in glass pots so you can watch the buds open.

places.name: Tea shops along Lijing Gate food street
places.note: Sell loose buds by weight and will brew a cup for you to taste first.

places.name: Kiosks at Luoyang National Peony Garden
places.note: Best in April when the gardens are in bloom and the tea is freshly packed.

landmarks: Longmen Grottoes
Over 100,000 Buddhist figures carved into riverside limestone cliffs across four centuries culminate in the serene 17-meter Vairocana Buddha, a UNESCO masterpiece.
White Horse Temple (Baima Si)
Founded in 68 AD, China's first Buddhist temple pairs ancient halls and pagodas with striking international shrines gifted by India, Thailand, and Myanmar.
Shaolin Temple and Pagoda Forest
A day trip to Mount Song reaches the legendary birthplace of Zen Buddhism and kung fu, where monks perform and 246 brick pagodas honor past masters.
Lijing Gate and Luoyang Old Town
The imposing rebuilt city gate opens onto lantern-strung lanes of street food, teahouses, and hanfu-clad visitors, magical when illuminated after dark.
Luoyang Museum
This sweeping modern museum showcases treasures from thirteen dynasties that ruled from Luoyang, including Tang sancai camels and exquisite bronzes.
Sui and Tang Luoyang City National Heritage Park
Reconstructed atop Empress Wu Zetian's palace ruins, the towering Mingtang and Tiantang halls resurrect the splendor of the Tang dynasty's eastern capital.
Guanlin Temple
Legendary general Guan Yu's head is said to rest beneath this cypress-shaded Ming temple complex, a major pilgrimage site for admirers of the god of war.
Wangcheng Park Peony Gardens
Luoyang is China's peony capital, and each April this vast park erupts in hundreds of varieties during the spectacular National Peony Festival.
Luoyang Ancient Tombs Museum (Luoyang Ancient Art Museum)
Descend into relocated burial chambers spanning nine dynasties, their original murals and brick carvings making this one of China's most unusual underground museums.
Guanyintang and Xiaolangdi Dam Scenic Area
North of the city, the Yellow River thunders through the Xiaolangdi Dam's spectacular annual silt-flushing releases amid reservoir and gorge scenery.

train.note: Luoyang has no international rail services - it is deep in central Henan, far from any frontier. The city has two stations: Luoyang Longmen for high-speed trains, with Zhengzhou in about 40 minutes, Xi'an in 1.5-2 hours, Beijing West in about 4 hours and Shanghai in 5-6 hours (or about 9 hours on the D-class sleeper), and the older Luoyang Station for conventional services, where Beijing takes 8-11 hours, Wuhan about 8 hours, Shanghai about 17 hours and Guangzhou around 24 hours. Longmen station is also the closest station to the Longmen Grottoes, which makes it the more convenient arrival point for most visitors. Book on 12306 with your passport.

bus.note: No international coaches run from Luoyang. Two main long-distance bus stations, both close to the old Luoyang railway station, serve Xi'an in around 5 hours and Zhengzhou in roughly 2 hours along with towns across western Henan. The high-speed train beats the bus on both of those routes, so coaches are mostly useful for smaller places such as Gongyi and the Shaolin Temple area near Dengfeng.

ferry.note: Luoyang sits on the Luo River in landlocked Henan province, several hundred kilometres from the coast, and neither the Luo nor the nearby Yellow River carries scheduled passenger boats.

half.name: Zhengzhou
half.blurb: Henan's provincial capital about an hour from Luoyang by high-speed train, home to the Henan Museum's collection of ancient bronzes and jades.

full.name: Kaifeng
full.blurb: A former imperial capital roughly 200 kilometers from Luoyang with the Song-dynasty Iron Pagoda and a preserved old city wall.

full.name: Yuntaishan Geopark
full.blurb: A UNESCO geopark about 150 kilometers from Luoyang with red sandstone gorges, waterfalls, and a narrow slot canyon called the Red Stone Gorge.
